evidence:
Scope: static source review of the frozen bytes; no Docker build, no configured judge run, no private checker executed. Workbook row 47 (Quality Checks D48): 'Shared pinned judge agent + model, pinned judge CLIs and browser, graded time rules on a fixed clock. Temperature and prompt-version markers are not required. Network is public here, so an open verifier network / missing allowlist is NOT a defect.' The Internal sheet's older wording (temperature 0, versioned prompt, no unpinned network) is superseded by that client-facing text and by SKILL.md delivery profile, so none of those were treated as defects. Skill procedure (quality-checks.md:187-189): judge agent, model, CLIs, browser and shared tools/ pinned; graded time rules on the fixed clock.

1. Judge agent + model: task/task.toml:30-35 is the frozen block exactly (REWARDKIT_JUDGE = "claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL = "z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx", ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api", ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}", ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = ""). A diff of task.toml against the frozen template shows only name/description/keywords/metadata lines differ; [verifier], [verifier.env] and timeouts are unchanged. All five judge.toml headers carry only judge = "claude-code", mode, timeout, isolated, prompt_template; a grep for model/reasoning/temperature keys outside descriptions returned nothing. test.sh:63-66 refuses to grade without both env values, so there is no silent fallback model.

2. Judge CLIs, browser, RewardKit: task/tests/Dockerfile:16-22 pins @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1; line 31 pins harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7; lines 33-38 install Chromium through the Playwright bundled inside the pinned @playwright/mcp and symlink it to /usr/local/bin/chromium, which every judge.toml passes as --executable-path. The rewardkit patch at line 41 asserts its anchor text, so it fails the build rather than drifting silently. tests/Dockerfile sha256 72998ab8... is byte-identical to the frozen template.

3. Shared tools: tests/tools/score.py (13de2b38...), tests/tools/restart_mcp.py (03c1426f...), tests/test.sh (bd682592...), tests/scoring.toml and tests/.dockerignore are byte-identical to the frozen template copies. Invariants also present by reading: score.py resolves parent.parent/scoring.toml (line 10), checks finite 0-1 (line 18), reports gates_passed/floors_passed/weighted_score; restart_mcp.py uses a .used marker (line 29), a sanitized env (line 40) and isError (line 80). The private check-canonical-shared-files.py was not run; comparison is against the template in the frozen rules folder, which is the only known build available here.

4. No trial-time fetch or install: test.sh contains no curl/wget/git clone/pip/npm; its only network calls are urllib probes of 127.0.0.1:3000 (lines 48, 136). The only wall-clock read is a log line in the restart helper (line 178), which is not graded.

5. Graded time rules on a fixed clock: the public note states the anchor (hireops_rules.md:59-61 'The system carries one stored reference moment, `2026-08-01T00:00:00Z`. Nothing in this app reads the operating system's clock'), the seed carries it (environment/assets/seed_data.json:3 "reference_moment": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"), and tests/app_context.md:27-28 restates it to every judge. Every date-dependent expectation I found is computed from that stored moment or from dates the judge types in: functional/judge.toml:614 (referral cliff vs 2026-08-01), 623 (future-start control), 587 (completed months from supplied start/effective instants), 560, 1154, 1163 (vesting from supplied instants), and prompt.md P4/P7/P8/B6. No criterion or prompt uses today, the run date, an age-relative value or a displayed creation time; judge.toml:812 says no timestamp is required. The 15-second live-update windows (judge.toml:1334/1343/1352, polish judge.toml:23) and the 3-second allowance are elapsed-time waits stated publicly (hireops_rules.md:521-522, instruction.md:9), not calendar rules, so they do not move with the run date.

Counterexample attempts. (a) Broken app that might pass: an app that reads the OS clock for the referral cliff. On any real run date after 2026-08-01 it reports the 2026-02-01T00:00:00.001Z referral as fully vested (10000.00) where line 614 expects 5000.00, so it is caught regardless of when the verifier runs. (b) Conforming app that might fail: one that stamps records with real wall-clock creation times. Nothing graded compares a creation time, so it is not penalised by a time rule. The golden itself stamps with the stored moment (solution/app/src/index.js:62 `const now = () => R.refAt(db);`) and grep found no Date.now/new Date() in it.

What the task does well: the millisecond-after-cliff case makes the fixed clock observable at any future run date instead of relying on the calendar.

Not measured, and not counted as defects under this row: (i) base images are tag-level (node:22-bookworm-slim, python:3.12-slim) and apt packages are unversioned; both are template-controlled bytes and the workbook treats unpinned apt as a NOTE; (ii) Chromium's exact build is pinned only transitively through @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 and I did not inspect that package's dependency spec; (iii) whether the OpenRouter slug resolves to one fixed provider build is outside the task and was not exercised; (iv) the raw evidence index contains scripted golden runs only, with no verifier image build log and no configured judge run, so nothing here confirms that the pinned versions install or that the judge launches. Those belong to rows 10/22 and the runtime records; this row's Pass rests on source bytes alone.
